title: The Tin Roof Rag
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: The Tin Roof Rag is a complete ragtime piano song in D major, in 4/4 time at 116 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Depot Platform Rag
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: The Depot Platform Rag is a complete ragtime piano song in E major, in 4/4 time at 116 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Cakewalk at the Church Social
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: Cakewalk at the Church Social is a complete ragtime piano song in F major, in 2/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Ferry Dock Rag
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: The Ferry Dock Rag is a complete ragtime piano song in D major, in 4/4 time at 116 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Ragtime Reunion
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Ragtime Reunion is a complete ragtime piano song in A major, in 2/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Cakewalk on a Winter Night
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Cakewalk on a Winter Night is a complete ragtime piano song in E major, in 4/4 time at 116 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Bandwagon Rag
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Bandwagon Rag is a complete ragtime piano song in C major, in 2/4 time at 100 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Two-Step at the Old Mill
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Two-Step at the Old Mill is a complete ragtime piano song in G major, in 4/4 time at 112 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Ragtime Farewell Parade
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Ragtime Farewell Parade is a complete ragtime piano song in F major, in 2/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is bright syncopation over a steady march-like bass. The A sections move through tonic, subdominant, tonic, dominant seventh, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.
